title: BitPacker: Enabling High Arithmetic Efficiency in Fully Homomorphic Encryption Accelerators
problem: The CKKS fully homomorphic encryption scheme uses integers of widely varying sizes (30-60 bits), leaving many bits unused in hardware registers and arithmetic datapaths. This poor bit utilization causes significant area and energy overheads in accelerators where multiplications dominate.
motivation: Efficient FHE computation on specialized hardware is essential to enable real-time performance on complex encrypted computations while maintaining cryptographic security.
method: CKKS encryption uses integers that vary widely in size, typically 30-60 bits each. When hardware multiplies these encrypted integers, they must fit into fixed-size registers, leaving many unused bits that waste silicon and power. BitPacker solves this by packing multiple encrypted integers together into the same arithmetic unit (the hardware that performs calculations), so fewer bits are wasted during each multiplication. This improves both the area efficiency and energy consumption of CKKS accelerators.
key_novelty: BitPacker efficiently packs variable-sized CKKS encrypted integers into arithmetic units to reduce wasted bits during multiplication operations.
contributions: BitPacker technique for improved bit packing of variable-sized FHE integers in hardware
Analysis of bit-wastage inefficiencies in CKKS accelerator designs
Demonstration of area and energy efficiency improvements through reduced wasted bits
